args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and find out why it was promoted even though the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west. The service was unhealthy, with an 18% error rate.
- **Version chosen:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, had also been unhealthy in staging.
- **After:** all three regions run v2.3.0. The service reports healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident INC-0001:** it describes the failure, the rollback and the result. It also lists two follow-ups: find what broke in v2.3.1, and find out why it was released even though its staging candidate was unhealthy.

The rollback went to a version that had been healthy in production before, so it didn't need change-manager approval.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
